transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-10-20 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 52m
- Recorders: Fireflies.ai

Summary: brief intro, technical scoping, security Qs, next steps

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for making time, i'm maya from redwood inference, joining with carlos our solutions eng and lena from security and tom on csm. how's everyone today?
[00:12] Priya (Customer CTO): good, thanks. big day for us, trying to nail down migration path from openai. we run clinical summarization + triage workflows so PHI is a big constraint.
[00:25] Evan (ML Eng): yeah and we also run internal embeddings for search and a few fine-tuned flows on top of gpt-4, some stuff on anthropic for safety checks.
[00:36] Carlos (Redwood SE): thanks, quick clarifying q — when you say "migration" is it full cutover or hybrid + fallback?
[00:43] Ava (PM): ideal is hybrid initially — run parity tests then route production traffic gradually. we want canary then a full switch if latency and quality match.
[00:52] Maya: cool. can you run through current infra and traffic? qps, typical prompt lengths, token mix?
[01:02] Ben (Platform): we're at about 180 rps during peak for short inference (avg 60 tokens), long-run summarization jobs ~12 rps at 800-1200 tokens. total monthly tokens ~2.3B.
[01:18] Evan: cost is getting hairy on openai, also authorization/enterprise controls are limited for us.
[01:26] Sofia (Security): and PHI: we need encryption at rest, KMS integration, audit logs, and SOC2 Type II — those are hard requirements.

--- Topics: compatibility ---
[01:40] Carlos: high level on compatibility — we can host open weights or run Redwood-hosted variants. curious: are you using vLLM or TGI in-house?
[01:49] Evan: we spike with vllm for batch jobs and use TGI in a dev cluster for model variants. production is mostly hosted api right now.
[01:57] Carlos: okay. Redwood's serving runtime supports model variants and has a compatibility layer for vLLM/TGI exported models, but there are caveats around custom operators and recent fp16 quant paths.
[02:10] Evan: caveats like?
[02:12] Carlos: sometimes custom fused kernels need recompilation or small code changes; kv cache behavior can differ which affects streaming latencies — we usually run a small conversion and a short benchmark to verify parity.
[02:24] Evan: that matches our fears. our devs built some custom runtime hooks for faster kv reuse. how invasive would porting be?
[02:31] Carlos: depends — most customers see 90-98% parity with minimal changes but the outliers are custom CUDA ops or unusual quantization formats. we can run the sample harness against your exported model; if needed we help with a tiny shim.

--- Topics: latency & cost tradeoffs ---
[02:45] Maya: about latency, you mentioned 60-token fast paths; what tail latency SLOs do you need?
[02:51] Ben: user-facing UI needs p95 <300ms for short responses. the summarization jobs can tolerate 1.5s-2s.
[02:59] Carlos: on Dedicated we can guarantee lower jitter via reserved GPU pools. Redwood Optimize will suggest batching/quantization tradeoffs — for example 4-bit quant + dynamic batching can reduce cost 2-3x but might add 50-150ms depending on the workload.
[03:13] Ava: is streaming affected by batching? some of our UIs rely on progressive tokens.
[03:18] Carlos: streaming still works — we do continuous batching and prefix cache to avoid blocking the first token. in practice you tune the max-latency window.

--- Topics: security / private deployment ---
[03:32] Sofia: PHI e2e: can we run in a VPC with customer KMS and bring-your-own-key? audits are mandatory.
[03:39] Lena (Redwood Security): yes — Private deployments support customer KMS/HSM, VPC peering, and we provide audit logs and SAML/SSO for RBAC. we have customers in regulated verticals.
[03:50] Sofia: and data residency? our legal requires EU processing for EU patients.
[03:55] Lena: we have regional options and can pin inference to regions. we'll include SOC2 and encryption details in the packet.

[04:06] Priya: how do you handle retention and delete requests? we need proof of deletion for certain datasets.
[04:12] Tom (CSM): retention is configurable per-tenant; for Private you control retention. for hosted we offer configurable retention windows and can support delete requests with audit trails. we'll include the exact process in the security packet.

--- Topics: eval parity & benchmarks ---
[04:30] Maya: let's talk about the parity plan — sounds like you want to run a benchmark harness against Redwood. we usually recommend a 2-week pilot: smoke, parity, performance, then canary.
[04:39] Evan: yes. we have sample prompts and an eval set for rouge/accuracy + safety checks. we also want to ensure our safety stack (anthropic checks) stays compatible.
[04:48] Carlos: on the safety piece, you can run a hybrid chain: generation on Redwood, safety checks either on Anthropic or local model. Redwood supports function/tool calling so you can insert your check as a step.
[04:58] Ava: what about hallucination differences and prompt-engineering drift? we can't afford regression on clinical outputs.
[05:05] Carlos: we run regression alerts tied to prompt sets in Redwood Optimize — you'll get quality monitoring, and we tie regression alerts to token-level diffs. for the pilot we'll baseline with your prompts and set acceptance thresholds.

--- Transcript noise / clarifications ---
[05:20] Speaker 2: (inaudible)
[05:23] Priya: sorry can you repeat the warranty on SLA?
[05:26] Maya: dedicated customers get SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we can go over specifics in the contract.

--- Tech deep dive preview ---
[05:35] Ben: on the technical deep dive, we want to verify model export formats — we've got both .safetensors and torch state dicts and some converted tgi artifacts. will that work?
[05:44] Carlos: we accept safetensors and torch; tgi exports often need a compatibility pass. bring sample artifacts to the deep dive. we'll attempt a quick local run and surface any missing ops.
[05:55] Evan: is there a recommended quantization path for us? we use an amp eval that works on fp16 currently.
[06:02] Carlos: 4-bit q (nf4/awq) is usually best for cost, but depends on model family. we'll provide per-model recommendations after we see the artifacts. for fp16 you can also do mixed precision which keeps latency low.

--- Cost modeling ---
[06:18] Maya: quick note on cost: we can model hosted per-token and dedicated committed pricing. with your volume committed Dedicated might be 20-40% cheaper depending on utilization. we'll share a TCO calculator.
[06:29] Ava: what's the minimum committed for Dedicated?
[06:31] Maya: we can propose a small PO for initial reserved capacity that covers your peak baseline; we'll include burst and autoscale policy in the proposal.

--- Risk and mitigations ---
[06:42] Sofia: my team wants to see pen-test and third-party attestation records — also process for regulatory subpoenas.
[06:49] Lena: we'll include pen-test summaries, SOC2 Type II report, and our legal team can walk through data subpoena processes in a follow-up.

--- Closing recap ---
[07:02] Maya: recap: 1) we'll send security pack (lena), 2) carlos will send benchmark harness + instructions, 3) i'll send pricing and dedicated template, 4) you (ntg) will send usage metrics. schedule tech-deep-dive for vllm/tgi compatibility.
[07:16] Priya: sounds good. target rapid turnaround — we'd like to run pilot in early november if possible.
[07:21] Maya: we'll try to hit those dates, thanks everyone.
[07:25] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker labels genericed, some words misheard (vLLM sometimes transcribed as v-l-m), timestamps approximate, natural speech fillers preserved.
